steps.text: Simplify the left side: \(\frac{12x+28}{4}=3x+7\), so the equation is \(3x+7-\frac{s}{13}=rx-8r\).
Infinitely many solutions means both sides are identical: the x-terms match, so \(r=3\).
The constants must match too: \(7-\frac{s}{13}=-8(3)=-24\).
So \(\frac{s}{13}=31\), which gives \(s=403\).
Line k has slope \(-\frac{17}{3}\).
A perpendicular slope is the negative reciprocal: flip the fraction and change the sign.
The slope of line j is \(\frac{3}{17}\) (or 0.1764).
To fit the most 120-pound packages, carry the fewest packages allowed: exactly 10.
Ten 100-pound packages weigh 1,000 pounds, leaving 100 pounds of room.
Each swap of a 100-pound package for a 120-pound one adds 20 pounds, so you can swap \(100÷20=5\) times.
The maximum is 5 packages of 120 pounds: choice C.
Slope from the table: \(\frac{-15-13}{(k+7)-k}=\frac{-28}{7}=-4\).
A y-intercept has x-coordinate 0, so \(k-5=0\) and \(k=5\). The point \((5,13)\) is on the line.
Go from \(x=5\) back to \(x=0\): that's 5 steps left, and each step left raises y by 4.
Type the first equation into Desmos.
Type the second equation.
Tap where the lines cross: the point is \((5,1.5)\).
So \(y=1.5\) (or \(\frac{3}{2}\)). By hand, adding the equations gives \(4y=6\) just as fast.
The first equation already tells you \(\frac{1}{2}y=4\).
Put 4 in place of \(\frac{1}{2}y\) in the second equation: \(x-4=2\).
So \(x=6\): choice D.
From the graph, line h crosses the axes at \((-6,0)\) and \((0,-9)\), so its slope is \(\frac{-9}{6}=-\frac{3}{2}\) and it is \(3x+2y=-18\).
No solution means line k is parallel to h but not the same line. Scale h so its y-term matches k's \(48y\): multiply by 24 to get \(72x+48y=-432\).
If \(t=-432\), line k would be exactly line h (infinitely many solutions), so t can be anything except \(-432\).
The value t cannot be is \(-432\): choice A.
Use the point with \(x=0\), since it makes the a-term disappear: \(a(0)+k(-3)=6\).
So \(-3k=6\) and \(k=-2\): choice A.
First equation: add \(\frac{3}{2}y\) to both sides to get \(3y-\frac{1}{4}x=\frac{2}{3}\). Multiply by \(-4\): \(x-12y=-\frac{8}{3}\).
Second equation: subtract \(\frac{3}{2}\) from both sides to get \(\frac{1}{2}x-py=3\). Multiply by 2: \(x-2py=6\).
No solution means the x- and y-coefficients match but the constants don't. The x-terms already match, so \(2p=12\).
So \(p=6\) (and the constants \(-\frac{8}{3}\) and 6 differ, as needed).
Rate: \(24000-19350=4650\) bushels in 5 hours, so 930 bushels per hour.
To get down to 12,840 bushels, the auger removes \(24000-12840=11160\) bushels in all.
Time: \(11160÷930=12\) hours: choice D.
Slope from the first two rows: \(\frac{160-130}{23-18}=\frac{30}{5}=6\).
Find the y-intercept: \(130=6(18)+b\), so \(b=22\) and line h is \(y=6x+22\).
Translating down 5 lowers the y-intercept by 5: line k is \(y=6x+17\).
Set \(y=0\): \(6x=-17\), so \(x=-\frac{17}{6}\). The x-intercept is \((-\frac{17}{6},0)\): choice D.
Going from 40 dollars to 60 dollars (up 20) drops demand by 5,000, so each dollar drops demand by 250.
55 dollars is 5 dollars below 60, so demand is \(5×250=1250\) higher than at 60 dollars.
Y-intercept: \(45=5(6)+b\), so \(b=15\) and the line is \(y=5x+15\).
Hiro: 4 shirts at x dollars and 2 pants at y dollars cost 86, so \(4x+2y=86\).
Sofia: 3 shirts and 5 pants cost 166, so \(3x+5y=166\).
That pair is choice A.
Put it in the second equation: \(-4(3)+y=-2\), so \(y=10\).
Test the easiest case: 1 day costs 270 dollars, so the right equation must give \(y=270\) when \(x=1\).
Only D works: choice D. (It's \(270+135(x-1)\) simplified.)
The height starts at 15 feet, so 15 is the constant term.
It rises 8 feet every second, so 8 multiplies s.
\(h=8s+15\): choice A.
Four times the body weight: \(4(0.5)=2\).
Add 0.6: \(2+0.6=2.6\) millimeters.
The solution to a system is the point where the two lines cross.
On the graph they cross at \(x=2\), \(y=3\).
The solution is \((2,3)\): choice C.
Don't solve for x. Notice \(3x+8\) is \(3x-8\) plus 16.
Solve for y: \(4y=-8x+6\), so \(y=-2x+\frac{3}{2}\). Line p has slope \(-2\).
A perpendicular slope is the negative reciprocal of \(-2\).
The slope of line r is \(\frac{1}{2}\) (or 0.5).
In \((8,10)\), the first number is x, the length, and the second is y, the width.
So the length is 8 m and the width is 10 m: choice C.
Taking the bus means waiting w minutes and then riding 5: \(w+5\) minutes in all.
Walking is faster when the bus total is more than the 20-minute walk.
\(w+5>20\): choice D.
\(f(5)=3\): choice C.
Infinitely many solutions means both equations are the same line.
First equation: \(y=\frac{4}{5}x+4+6=\frac{4}{5}x+10\).
Second equation: \(y=\frac{4}{5}x+8+v\).
Match the intercepts: \(8+v=10\), so \(v=2\): choice B.
Each time x goes up 17, y goes up 23, so the slope is \(\frac{23}{17}\) (positive).
At \(x=0\), \(y=t+46\), so that's the y-intercept.
\(y=\frac{23}{17}x+t+46\): choice D.
The equation counts pans, not inches, so the sizes 10, 9 and 7 don't multiply anything.
Pans: \(4n\) ten-inch, \(n\) nine-inch and 10 seven-inch, which add to 100.
In \(f(12)=0\), the input 12 is hours and the output 0 is muffins left.
So after 12 hours there are no free muffins left.
It takes 12 hours to give them all away: choice C.
The point \((0,3)\) gives the y-intercept: 3.
\(f(x)=4x+3\): choice C.
84 less than x means start with x and subtract 84.
\(y=x-84\): choice D.
Put 90 in for x and type the equation into Desmos as it is.
Desmos draws a horizontal line, and its height is the answer: \(y=210\).
Start from the original price, 690 dollars.
Take away 150 dollars for each of the t years: \(150t\).
A linear equation has exactly one solution unless the x-coefficients on both sides are equal.
The x-coefficients are \(r-9\) and 19. They're equal when \(r-9=19\), so \(r=28\).
With \(r=28\) the x-terms cancel and there is no solution, so r cannot be 28: choice D.
The slopes are 1 and 8, which are different.
Two lines with different slopes always cross at exactly one point: choice B.
Substitute \(y=3x\) into the second equation: \(2x+3x=12\).
That's already \(5x=12\), which is exactly what's asked: choice C.
Red beads in the first container: 30% of x is \(0.3x\). In the second: \(0.7y\).
At least 400 red beads means the total is greater than or equal to 400.
Check \(x=0\): the equation gives \(y=0+4=4\).
Only the table in choice A has \(y=4\) when \(x=0\), and its other rows (1, 5) and (2, 6) also fit: choice A.
Each cubic yard of topsoil (x) costs 24.50 dollars, and each ton of stone (y) costs 24.75 dollars.
\(24.75-24.5=0.25\), so a ton of stone costs 0.25 dollars more.
Track the salt. The low-salt mixture gives \(0.02x\) kilograms and the high-salt one gives \(0.96y\).
The final 24 kilograms are 4% salt: \((0.04)(24)\) kilograms.
\(4b=16\), so \(b=4\) large boxes: choice B.
Pretend all 60 tents hold 4 people: that's 240 spots, but only 202 people went.
That's 38 spots too many, and switching one tent from 4-person to 2-person removes 2 spots.
\(38÷2=19\) tents are 2-person tents: choice C.
Profit = revenue minus fixed costs, and the equation is \(15000=2.00x-4500\).
4,500 is subtracted, so it's the fixed costs. That leaves \(2.00x\) as the revenue.
It's 2 dollars per dispenser times x dispensers: the monthly revenue from x dispensers, choice A.
Count tickets: \(s+p=250\).
Count money: standard tickets bring 5 dollars each and premium tickets 12, so \(5s+12p=2300\).
That pair is choice A.
Divide the given equation by 38: \(x-n=y+n\), which is \(x-y=2n\).
No solution needs a parallel line (same \(x-y\) on the left) with a different constant.
A divides to \(x-y=2n\), the same line. D divides to \(x-y=n\), which is parallel and different because \(n>0\).
Choice D.
Widest spaces (9 feet) give the fewest: \(135÷9=15\).
Narrowest spaces (7.5 feet) give the most: \(135÷7.5=18\).
So \(15≤n≤18\): choice D.
x is minutes running and y is minutes biking, so \(x+y\) is the total.
75 is the total minutes spent running and biking each day: choice C.
Subtract 4x and add 29: \(2x=23\), so \(x=\frac{23}{2}\).
Gas cost per mile: \(\frac{1}{25}\) gallon at 4 dollars a gallon is \(\frac{4}{25}\) dollars per mile.
Driving m fewer miles saves \(\frac{4}{25}m\) dollars, and he wants to save 5 dollars.
\(\frac{4}{25}m=5\): choice D.
Divide everything by 7 first: \(g+b=120\).
With 71 blue tiles: \(g=120-71=49\) green tiles.
Test each choice in both inequalities; it must make both true.
Only C and D have slope \(-\frac{1}{3}\). Check which one passes through \((9,10)\).
Choice D.
The tree starts at 6 feet, and \(2n\) is the height added over n years.
So 2 is the feet it grows each year on average: choice B.
Factor the left side: \(2x+16=2(x+8)\).
Then \(2(x+8)=a(x+8)\) is true for every x exactly when \(a=2\).
\((0,9)\) gives the y-intercept: 9.
From \(x=0\) to \(x=1\), y goes from 9 to 17, so the slope is 8.
\(y=8x+9\): choice D.
If \(b-2=0\), the equation becomes \(0=8\), which is never true.
So \(b=2\) gives no solution: choice A.
Slope 4 and y-intercept 6 (from the point \((0,6)\)).
\(y=4x+6\): choice D.
x is the number of triangles and y the number of rectangles.
\((24,73)\) means 24 triangles and 73 rectangles: choice A.
Find the original y-intercept by setting \(x=0\): \(33y=297\), so \(y=9\).
Shifting down 5 units moves it to \(9-5=4\).
The new y-intercept is \((0,4)\): choice A.
The pass beats tickets soonest when every trip is the most expensive kind, 3.50 dollars.
The smallest whole number of trips is 28.
4 trays hold at least \(4×50=200\) and at most \(4×60=240\) cookies.
The only choice from 200 to 240 is 205: choice B.
Expand both sides: left is \(150x-90\), right is \(-90+150x\).
They're exactly the same expression, so every x works.
Infinitely many solutions: choice C.
Put 0 in for x: \(g(0)=-0+8\).
\(g(0)=8\): choice D.
Don't solve for x: the question wants \(5x\), which is already inside the parentheses.
Divide both sides by 2: \(5x=3\): choice C.
The session lasted 30 minutes, so put 30 in for x.
\(y=0.1(30)=3\) pieces: choice B.
Distribute: \(9r=7r+49\).
The cost per additional mile is the slope of the line.
The line starts at 3 dollars at 0 miles and is at 5 dollars at 1 mile.
It rises 2 dollars per mile: choice A.
The x-intercept is where \(y=0\), meaning no cargo is left.
So all the cargo is moved in about 4.8 hours: choice A.
The line crosses the y-axis at \(-1\), so the y-intercept is \(-1\). That leaves A or D.
It crosses the x-axis at \(-4\): going 4 right from there, it drops 1. The slope is \(-\frac{1}{4}\).
\(y=-\frac{1}{4}x-1\): choice A.
First equation: subtract 10y to get \(4x-16y=2\), then halve it: \(2x-8y=1\).
Second equation: rearrange to \(2x-ty=-\frac{1}{2}\).
No solution means matching x and y coefficients with different constants: \(t=8\) (and 1 ≠ \(-\frac{1}{2}\)).
\(h(0)=0\) means there is no constant term: the line goes through the origin.
\(h(x)=\frac{10}{11}x\): choice A.
The line is \(y=5x-35\).
At the x-intercept, \(y=0\): \(5x=35\), so \(x=7\).
F is linear with slope \(\frac{9}{5}\): each kelvin adds \(\frac{9}{5}\) degrees Fahrenheit. The 273.15 and 32 don't matter for a change.
Increase: \(\frac{9}{5}(9.10)=16.38\) degrees: choice A.
Multiply both sides by 5: \(4x=100\).
Divide by 4: \(x=25\): choice A.
Find each line's easy points. \(x+5y=5\) passes through \((0,1)\) and \((5,0)\): a shallow line.
\(2x-y=-4\) passes through \((0,4)\) and \((-2,0)\): a steep line.
Only graph C has a steep line through \((-2,0)\) and \((0,4)\) and a shallow one through \((0,1)\): choice C.
If \(x<0\) and \(y>0\), then \(5x\) is negative and \(-7y\) is negative too.
So \(5x-7y\) is negative there, and can never be greater than 35.
That region has no solutions: choice D.

Divide time by distance in the first row: \(8÷0.32=25\).
Check another row: \(14÷0.56=25\). So \(t=25d\): choice C.
Session 1 is free and session 2 costs half of 25.40, which is 12.70 dollars.
The other \(x-2\) sessions cost 25.40 dollars each.
Divide every term of \(4x+6=12\) by 2.
\(2x+3=6\): choice D.
Caroline's charge more than Adam's: \(17+10x>20+9.5x\).
Subtract: \(0.5x>3\), so \(x>6\): choice D.
Start at the x-intercept \((-6,0)\) and move 6 units right to reach \(x=0\).
With slope \(-\frac{5}{3}\), y changes by \(-\frac{5}{3}(6)=-10\).
The y-intercept's y-coordinate is \(-10\).
\(x+y=10\): choice D.
Each pound costs 2 dollars.
c pounds cost 2 dollars c times: \(2c\), choice A.
The line starts at 100 dollars (the system) and reaches 200 dollars at 4 games.
Slope: \(\frac{200-100}{4}=25\) dollars per game.
The slope means each game costs 25 dollars: choice A.
After the first 3 hours, the train drives \(x-3\) more hours at 53 miles per hour.
\(y=53x+14\): choice B.
In the first hour he covers \(60(1)=60\) miles, leaving \(210-60=150\) miles.
At 50 miles per hour that takes \(150÷50=3\) hours, so \(y=3\).
Exactly one solution needs a line with a different slope from \(x+y=20\).
A, B and C are all multiples of \(x+y\) on the left, so they're parallel (or the same line).
\(x-y=20\) has a different slope: choice D.

The solution is \((1,5)\): choice B.
The solution is where the two lines cross.
They cross at \(x=3\), \(y=9\): choice A.
Don't solve for x: treat \(2(x-8)\) as one block.

The x-intercept is where \(h(x)=0\): \(x+12=0\), so \(x=-12\).
Every flag is blue or yellow, 25 in all.
\(25-20=5\) yellow flags: choice A.
Hours running: \(\frac{r}{5}\). Hours biking: \(\frac{b}{10}\). Biking time is twice running time: \(\frac{b}{10}=\frac{2r}{5}\), so \(b=4r\).
Total miles: \(r+4r=200\), so \(r=40\).
She biked \(b=4(40)=160\) miles: choice D.

Divide both sides by 8.

Subtract 2: \(-45-2=-47\): choice A.

Divide by 9: \(x+y=18\): choice C.

\(y=5x+6\): choice A.
Test a point from the table in the choices. Use \((3,38)\).
Choice A.

\(f(x)=-2x+8\): choice B.
At most 2 less than 3 times y: \(x≤3y-2\).
The greatest possible x is \(-14\).

\(x=3\) means 3 months after September 1: December 1.

\(f(x)=4x+2\): choice C.

Only the x-terms affect the slope: \(\frac{29}{3}x+5x\).
The mean of four exams is their sum divided by 4.
It must be at least 90: \(\frac{G+85+78+98}{4}≥90\): choice C.
Infinitely many solutions means the second equation is the first one scaled.
The second has \(1y\), so multiply the first by 3: \(\frac{3}{2}x+y=\frac{1}{2}\).
So \(a=\frac{3}{2}\): choice D.
The graph shown is \(y=f(x)+14\). It crosses the y-axis at 2 and the x-axis at 8, so its slope is \(-\frac{2}{8}=-\frac{1}{4}\).
Subtract 14: \(f(x)=-\frac{1}{4}x-12\): choice A.
